approach: Root cause: the reading gate fixes criteria from the request text, and no step compares each criterion with the defaults that govern how criteria are judged (D43's rule that a behavior criterion uses only commands the verifier can run, D115, and the append-only rule for docs/decisions.md and records/). Fix it at the gate. Add `check_judging_rules` to reading/surveys.rs: it reads only the parsed criteria and the deliverable list and costs no model call. Register it as the last `step!` in `refusing_check` (checks.rs), so no existing check changes which reading it refuses first. It refuses (a) a behavior criterion whose cited command the verifier cannot run: `cargo fmt` without `--check`, `cargo install|publish|fix` or `--fix`, a git write command or an environment-variable prefix in a backticked simple command; (b) a criterion that edits an existing decision entry in place or a file under `records/`; (c) a deliverable under `records/`, or a Delete of docs/decisions.md. A Modify of docs/decisions.md is accepted, because appending is a Modify. The error names the criterion number and text and says what to write instead: a command the verifier can run, or a new appended decision that amends the old one. Wire in the corpus cases, the unit tests in reading.rs, the 13th reader-rule line and the briefs.rs tests, a new D174 appended at the end of the log (amends D43), a decision-links entry, and a CHANGELOG entry.

decisions.choice: The step is the last one in refusing_check, after check_reading_references.
decisions.reason: Existing tests assert which check refuses first (reading.rs:5107 expects check_environment_reach, run_pin_tests.rs:1918 and :1985 expect check_criteria_evidence). A last position leaves all of those unchanged. The check is also the broadest, so it should run only after the specific ones accept.

rejected.option: Place it right after check_criteria_evidence, next to the other evidence check
rejected.why: It would take over the refusal of readings that check_environment_reach and later checks refuse today, and so change the rule name recorded for them.

decisions.choice: Match narrowly, on parsed criterion text. Commands are read from backticked spans split on `&&`, `||`, `;` and `|`; `cargo fmt|install|publish|fix` are also read from bare text. Decision edits need a decision id (D plus 1-3 digits) or an 'existing/in place' phrase next to docs/decisions.md, with an edit verb within 4 words. A `records/` token needs an edit verb in the 3 words before it, and none of 'from', 'read' or 'reads'. A criterion containing a word that starts 'refus' or 'reject', or the word 'append', 'appends', 'appending', 'supersede', 'supersedes', 'amend' or 'amends', is exempt. Commands in prose outside backticks, other than cargo fmt|install|publish|fix, are not read.
decisions.reason: A criterion that only describes the rule is not a violation. This job's own criterion 1 names `cargo fmt` without --check and an in-place D87 edit, and says each is refused, so it needs the 'refus*' exemption or it would be refused when re-read or replayed. Criterion 8 says 'appending' and reading.rs:7108 says 'records/ is not changed', and both must stay accepted. Reading git or records names in prose (a criterion about the records writer, or one saying a helper runs git commit) must not be refused.

rejected.option: Scan the whole criterion text for any git write verb or the word records/
rejected.why: Criteria for athena-git or the records writer would be refused wrongly.

rejected.option: Refuse every Modify deliverable on docs/decisions.md
rejected.why: Every legitimate append is a Modify, and this job's own deliverables list it. Acceptance criterion 2 requires that an append-only deliverable is accepted.

risks.risk: The matcher refuses a legitimate criterion, for example one that describes a git or cargo command in prose or backticks as part of the feature under test.
risks.mitigation: Commands are read from backticked simple commands, and only the cargo subcommands fmt, install, publish and fix are read from bare text. A criterion with a word starting 'refus' or 'reject' is exempt. The accept tests and the accept corpus cases cover the common shapes. The error names the criterion and the repair.

risks.risk: Known misses: a git write command written in prose without backticks; a bad criterion that adds the word 'refuse' or 'append' to dodge the check; an edit written without a decision id or the 'existing/in place' wording; records/ edited through a phrase with more than three words before the path.
risks.mitigation: These are named in the doc comment and D174 as limits. The check blocks the observed instances and their common phrasings, and the verifier and D43's judge remain a second layer.

risks.risk: The rules section of the reader brief is at or near its 3045-byte baseline, so a new 13th line can fail the size test. I did not measure the current size.

risks.risk: A wrong line number in decision-links.toml or an extra 'supersedes/amends Dnn' phrase in D174 fails the decisions tests, and decision-links.toml is not in the same file as the line it points at.
risks.mitigation: Write the 'Amends D43' line once, find its number with Grep on docs/decisions.md, and put that number in the link. Use 'supersede' and 'amend' with no trailing s elsewhere. cargo test -p athena-cli decisions shows any mismatch.

risks.risk: The real share of newly refused readings is not measured. The planner snapshot has no records, so 3% is an estimate.
risks.mitigation: Declare 'expected 3% of newly refused readings' as an estimate in the doc, changelog, D174 and criterion 5. The replay at verification measures it.

demonstrations.method: The new unit tests in crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs all have names starting `judging_rules_`. They build readings with the existing helpers `reading_with_criterion` (reading.rs:4461, Behavior kind), `governed_reading` (:4558) and `add_behavior` (:4705), and call two entry points. One is `check_judging_rules` directly, to check that the error text names 'criterion N' and the criterion text. The other is `refusing_check` through `gate_refuser` (:7206), to check that the refusing check's name is `check_judging_rules`. Refused: Behavior 'Run `cargo fmt`: the tree is formatted'; bare 'cargo fmt passes'; 'Run `cargo install athena`: it works'; 'Run `RUSTFLAGS=-D warnings cargo test`: passes'; 'Run `git commit -am x`: a commit exists'; Content 'Edit the existing D87 entry in docs/decisions.md in place so it names the new check'; 'Rewrite D87 to say X'; 'Correct records/jobs/x/outcome.json to say landed'; a deliverable `records/jobs/x/outcome.json`; and Delete of docs/decisions.md. Each case also asserts that adding a repair leaves no refusal.
demonstrations.observes: Every refused reading gives Some("check_judging_rules") from gate_refuser and an error that contains the criterion number and text. The error also has the repair advice (a command the verifier can run, or 'append a new decision' that amends the old one).

demonstrations.method: A content check, with a test modelled on `scope_limit_doc_and_changelog_name_the_cause` (reading.rs:8904). It reads checks.rs and surveys.rs through include_str! and asserts four things. `refusing_check` has exactly one `step!(check_judging_rules(reading));` line and it is last. The `check_reading_acceptance` doc in checks.rs links [`check_judging_rules`] and contains the root-cause sentence 'criteria are not tested against D43 and the append-only rules' with the ids 20261024-045548-7qht and 20261102-005332-8gkv. The `//` comment above the step line names the same cause and jobs. The doc comment of `check_judging_rules` in surveys.rs contains 'This check refuses more readings; the higher refusal rate is intended.' and 'expected 3% of newly refused readings'. Also run `Grep step!\(check_judging_rules crates/athena-core/src/reading/checks.rs`.
demonstrations.observes: One step line, positioned after check_reading_references, and the doc and comment text found.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the step line, the doc text or the job ids, the test's assertions fail.
demonstrations.seam: Reads source files with include_str!, the same way reading.rs:8908 does (exists). The test is added by step 5.

demonstrations.method: A test in refusal_corpus.rs modelled on `records_measure_refusal_is_declared_intended` (:3138). `athena_core::reading::replay_declaration` is called on a criterion with 'expected 3% of newly refused readings' and returns share Some(3). It is called again on the doc comment of `check_judging_rules` and the CHANGELOG item, which return the same share. The test also asserts that the changelog and D174 state 'higher refusal rate is intended' and call 3% an estimate, not a measurement, because the planner snapshot has no records to replay.
demonstrations.observes: A declared share of 3 in the criterion, the doc comment, the changelog item and D174.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the doc, changelog or D174 omit the declaration, the replay would hold the job above 10% newly refused, and this test fails.
demonstrations.seam: Production function `replay_declaration` (exists, called at refusal_corpus.rs:3140). The doc comment text is read with include_str! as at :3152. The test is added by step 6.

demonstrations.method: Step 4 edits `READING_RULES` in reader.rs (the array length goes from 12 to 13) and the test at briefs.rs:3625. The test now expects 13 lines, adds "check_judging_rules" to its list of check names, and asserts that one rule line names `check_judging_rules` together with 'D43' and 'append'. It keeps the 220-byte line cap and the section bounds (`READING_RULES_BASELINE_BYTES` and 3150). Also run `cargo test -p athena-cli --test budgets` for the token budgets and the system-facts line `budget reader: 1998 of 2000`.
demonstrations.observes: The reader brief shows 13 rule lines, one of them naming check_judging_rules. The section bytes are within the bounds. The reader budget line is unchanged, because the rule list is outside BudgetSet::Reader (lib.rs:285).
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the new rule line, the length assertion (13) and the name assertion fail. Without shortening the existing lines, the section-size assertions fail.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry point `reader_brief` (exists), with the test's own `reader_inputs(&reading())` fixture (exists, used at briefs.rs:3626).

demonstrations.method: Run the three checks Athena runs on the result. `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked` are run alongside this command. The workspace test run includes the decisions append-only guard (`the_decision_log_is_well_formed_and_only_appended_to`, decisions.rs:247), the decision-links tests (decisions.rs:413-414 and :483), the mirror rule for decision entries (mirrors.rs:354), the ontology and buy_first tests that read docs/decisions.md, the budgets test, and every test that calls check_reading_acceptance (reading.rs and replay.rs:55).
demonstrations.observes: All pass. D174 is the next id after D173, has a Provenance bullet and sits after the pinned bytes. Its single 'Amends D43' line number equals the new [[link]] line.
demonstrations.fails_without: A malformed D174, a wrong link line, a clippy warning, or a regression in an existing test makes the corresponding job fail.
demonstrations.seam: Existing test suites. The only fixture change is the one `git push` case moved out of the loop at reading.rs:5089-5116 by step 5.

demonstrations.method: The decisions.rs guard confirms the first 359622 bytes of docs/decisions.md still hash to the pinned value and that D174 is the next id. A content check by Read and Grep: CHANGELOG.md has a new bullet at the top of `### Added` under `## [Unreleased]` naming `reading::check_judging_rules`, the root cause, both job ids, the 'higher refusal rate is intended' sentence, 'expected 3% of newly refused readings', and the examples the check refuses. `git diff` of docs/decisions.md shows only added lines at the end.
demonstrations.observes: The pinned prefix is unchanged, with the new entry appended after D173. The changelog item is present.
demonstrations.fails_without: An in-place edit of any earlier entry changes the pinned prefix hash and fails the guard.
demonstrations.seam: Existing guard `check_log` (decisions.rs:218, exists). The files are edited by step 7.
